We are raising our full-year operating earnings per diluted share guidance, representing a 9 percent increase at the midpoint from our previously disclosed 2026 guidance, as discussed below.
We expect operating earnings per diluted share to be in the range of $5.05 to $5.15, excluding any significant items in the year (as compared to our previous guidance of $4.60 to $4.80).

We expect our expense ratio to be in the range of 18.6 percent to 18.8 percent (as compared to our previous guidance of 18.8 percent to 19.0 percent), reflecting improved operating leverage from continued strong sales results.
We expect fee income of approximately $25 million (compared to our previous guidance of $30 million), primarily reflecting the continued shift from Medicare Advantage to Medicare Supplement.

We expect the effective tax rate to be approximately 20.5 percent (as compared to our previous guidance of 21.5 percent), which excludes the impact resulting from the valuation allowance recognized during the current quarter.
Our 2026 operating ROE is expected to exceed the three-year target of 12 percent we had previously established for year-end 2027.
We expect to establish new operating ROE targets when we update our outlook in February 2027.
We are narrowing the range of our expected free cash flows to a range of $220 million to $240 million (as compared to our previous guidance of $200 million to $250 million).

We expect to continue to manage to: (i) a consolidated RBC ratio in the range of 360 percent to 390 percent for our U.S. based insurance subsidiaries; (ii) minimum holding company liquidity of $150 million; and (iii) a target debt to total capital, excluding accumulated other comprehensive loss, in the range of 25 percent to 28 percent.
We expect to spend approximately $70 million in 2026, which is largely consistent with our 2026 expectations.

Our RBC ratio at September 30, 2026 was within our targeted RBC ratio range of 360 percent to 390 percent that is reflected in our risk appetite statement that we share and discuss with rating agencies and insurance regulators.
We believe that the target RBC ratio range continues to adequately support our financial strength and credit ratings.
On April 8, 2026, AM Best affirmed its "A" financial strength ratings of our primary insurance subsidiaries and the outlook for these ratings remains stable.
Accordingly, downgrades and outlook revisions related to us or the life insurance industry may occur in the future at any time and without notice by any rating agency.
At September 30, 2026, CNO, CDOC and our other non-insurance subsidiaries held $230.7 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, which was above our minimum target level of $150 million.

We expect to receive regulatory approval for future dividends from our subsidiaries, but there can be no assurance that such payments will be approved or that the financial condition of our insurance subsidiaries will not change, making future approvals less likely.
The Company expects to deploy its free cash flow into investments to accelerate profitable growth, common stock dividends and share repurchases.

The amount and timing of future share repurchases (if any) will be based on business and market conditions and other factors including, but not limited to, available free cash flow, the current price of our common stock and investment opportunities.
On April 8, 2026, AM Best affirmed its "bbb" rating on our issuer credit and senior unsecured debt and the outlook for these ratings is stable.
